text:
noah: hey team, day 1 q: can someone outline the safest pattern for using hosted vs sandbox keys for a public demo? also curious if hosted key usage is audited (who called what) so we can show security to stakeholders.
maya: welcome! :wave: short answer: do not use permanent hosted prod keys in demos that touch public networks. For demos, request a short-lived hosted dev key scoped to the demo and timeboxed. Sandbox is fine for small demos but has tight quotas and lower concurrent streams.
noah: how do we request the short-lived hosted dev key and what info do they need?
devex-bot: open the quota/key request form: https://internal.redwood.devex/requests/keys. Include team name, demo window (start/end UTC), expected RPS/concurrent streams, models, and whether streaming is required. Mark as "demo" for expedited handling. Typical SLA ~24-48h.
aj: about auditing: hosted keys are logged. Console and audit logs show key usage, IPs, and per-request metadata. If you need more detailed logs for stakeholders, request an "audit export" when you open the key request and we can provide a short report for the demo window.
noah: great. one more: can CI gate on remaining quota so our e2e demo jobs skip if close to limit?
maya: yes 1 use the account limits endpoint or read response headers (X-RateLimit-Remaining). Gate heavy jobs when remaining < threshold. We usually skip (not fail) demo prechecks and surface a notice.
ops-bot: tip: for public demos prefer a replay approach (recorded responses) or a short-lived hosted dev key plus a caching proxy in front of the API to absorb bursts. For streaming-heavy demos, request concurrency explicitly.
noah: thanks all, i'll open the request with demo details and ask for an audit export. appreciate the help :thumbsup:
